title: FAA DRPDS diagnostic prerequisite model

semantics.unknowns_policy: Do not infer equipment instances, wiring, terminals, ratings, settings, or physical test points.

questions.title: Are the two documented commercial sources independent at the facility supply boundary?
questions.applicability: The historical FAA reference describes two independent three-phase commercial sources. Treat that as the reference architecture claim, not proof of a named site's current upstream utility topology. Confirm independence from current site one-line diagrams and utility records where available; do not invent upstream substations, shared buses, or utility arrangements.

questions.title: Is each documented commercial transformer providing supported input/output evidence to its corresponding SWGR incomer?
questions.applicability: The historical reference describes two commercial sources, one transformer per source, transformer input/output and protection evidence, and the corresponding 1M1/2M1 incomers. The 480/277 V grounded-wye secondary is a typical-reference detail only; primary voltage, rating, impedance, protection implementation and installed test points remain site-specific. No numeric acceptance limits or field test procedure are defined.

questions.title: Is a commercial source unavailable?
questions.applicability: Assess each documented commercial source at its source boundary. Separate actual source condition from instrument, sensing-fuse and telemetry faults. Transformer input/output and corresponding incomer evidence are assessed in the downstream transformer-path question; site-specific source boundaries and approved measurement methods must be verified.

questions.title: Can the documented generator start and reach its run/ready state?
questions.applicability: The reference identifies start circuits, starting batteries, fuel, lubrication, temperature, coolant, controller and alarms. Individual generator tags, detailed start permissives, thresholds and approved test procedures are not modeled; use only documented installed evidence.

questions.title: Has the running generator reached acceptable electrical output conditions?
questions.applicability: The reference states that the first generator reaching nominal speed and voltage connects to the common bus and identifies voltage/frequency monitoring. No numeric acceptance limits, individual terminals or installed sensing channels are supplied; these require current site records.

questions.title: Has the generator synchronized with and connected to the common generator bus?
questions.applicability: The reference describes the first qualified generator connecting to a common bus and subsequent units synchronizing. It does not provide synchronization limits, breaker tags, detailed interlocks or a site sequence. No switching or synchronization procedure is defined.

questions.title: Is the connected generator fleet sufficient for the documented load condition?
questions.applicability: The historical reference describes load shedding until enough generators are operating and later restoration, and gives a typical redundancy count with a facility exception. Do not encode that typical count as a universal threshold; the installed site's load, capacity, reserve and load-priority criteria are required.

questions.title: Is generator capacity electrically available?
questions.applicability: Umbrella assessment. Localize each unit through start/readiness, electrical output, synchronization/connection and fleet capacity/load response. Apply installed-unit and capacity conclusions only with current site equipment identity, load demand and approved operating criteria.

questions.title: Is the auxiliary control-power subsystem available for the required control functions?
questions.applicability: Evaluate when control, switching, alarm, or telemetry behavior may depend on the documented AC/DC auxiliary supply.

questions.title: Is the relevant SWGR section supplied from its intended source?
Did a main SWGR section transfer to standby?
questions.applicability: Only when the operating mode or observed event requires a transfer to standby supply.

questions.title: Is the documented essential switchboard feeder available to supply its assigned downstream section or load group?
questions.applicability: The documented essential path includes switchgear, switchboards, MCCs, outgoing feeders and loads. Apply to an individual feeder only after current site drawings and schedules establish its identity and assignment.

questions.title: Is the relevant MCC protective and control path available for its assigned motor load?
questions.applicability: The reference identifies MCCs, motor feeders, protection, contactors and local control as diagnostic layers. Individual MCC sections, feeder tags, control logic and protective settings require site drawings and equipment schedules.

questions.title: Is the assigned essential load responding as expected when its supply and control path are available?
questions.applicability: The reference lists cooling, pumps, chillers, compressors, fans, lighting and receptacles as essential loads and notes that some equipment has its own restart restrictions. Apply only to a documented load; do not infer restart timers or equipment-specific settings.

questions.title: Did essential-load shedding and restoration correspond to the documented generator-capacity condition?
questions.applicability: The historical reference describes automatic shedding of part of the essential load while generator capacity is insufficient and restoration as additional generators become available. The site's actual thresholds, priorities, feeder identities and sequence must come from current approved records; this question does not define or authorize switching.

questions.title: Is an essential load unavailable because of its supply path?
questions.applicability: Umbrella assessment. Localize an essential-load interruption through the switchboard feeder, MCC protective/control path and assigned load response. Assess generator-related load shedding/restoration separately when the event occurred during standby operation.

questions.title: Is the documented incoming supply path to the UPS supply switchgear available?
questions.applicability: The critical distribution architecture includes an UPS supply switchgear between the main SWGR and UPS equipment. Assess only incoming sources and switching elements identified by current site one-line drawings; the generic model does not establish the number, tags, or pairing of UPS SWGR incomers.

questions.title: Is the documented UPS SWGR outgoing feeder supplying the assigned UPS input?
questions.applicability: The diagnostic boundary separates UPS SWGR distribution from the UPS input itself. Apply to an individual feeder only when current site one-line drawings and equipment schedules establish its tag and assigned UPS; do not infer feeder count, breaker IDs, or source pairing.

questions.title: Are the documented UPS rectifier and inverter conversion functions available?
questions.applicability: Assess rectifier and inverter evidence separately for an identified UPS after its documented input feeder is assessed. Status names, internal design, thresholds and test methods are model-specific; do not infer an internal circuit topology or physical test points from the family-level architecture.

questions.title: Is the documented UPS bypass function and its selected supply path available?
questions.applicability: Assess only bypass functions and source paths identified for the installed UPS. The historical UPS 1 reserve role is a typical functional role, not proof of a particular site's bypass arrangement. Do not infer static/maintenance bypass implementation, switching sequence, interlocks or physical test points.

questions.title: Is the UPS DC bus and battery subsystem able to support the documented operating requirement?
questions.applicability: Evaluate the UPS DC bus and battery subsystem separately from the 125 V DC control-power system. Battery string/cell detail, charger arrangement, ratings, autonomy criteria and test procedures require installed equipment records and manufacturer/site-approved documentation.

questions.title: Is a UPS maintaining the intended critical supply mode?
Is the documented UPS 1 bypass-reserve role available to support UPS 2 and UPS 3?
questions.applicability: Applies only to the historical typical architecture where UPS 1 is documented as the bypass reserve for UPS 2 and UPS 3; the installed site's bypass design and operating procedure must be verified separately.

questions.title: Is the documented UPS 2 output path to Critical Bus A available?
questions.applicability: The UPS 2 to Critical Bus A assignment is a historical typical role; verify the installed site's equipment assignment and topology before applying.

questions.title: Is the documented UPS 3 output path to Critical Bus B available?
questions.applicability: The UPS 3 to Critical Bus B assignment is a historical typical role; verify the installed site's equipment assignment and topology before applying.

questions.title: Is Critical Bus A or B available?
Is a PDU distribution path available?
Is the documented incoming supply to the individual PDU available?
questions.applicability: Assess an individual PDU only after its installed identity and upstream Critical Bus A/B assignment are established from current site drawings. The historical reference describes 480/277 V three-wire input, but this is not proof of the installed PDU's nominal voltage, wiring, or measurement point.

questions.title: Is the documented PDU voltage-conversion function available?
questions.applicability: The historical reference describes conversion from 480/277 V three-wire input to 208/120 V four-wire output. Treat those values as reference-architecture data only; use current site schedules and manufacturer documentation for installed nominal values, conversion technology, phase configuration, acceptance limits and approved observation methods.

questions.title: Are the documented PDU internal switching and protective functions available and in the expected state?
questions.applicability: This question covers only PDU main/internal switching and protective functions identified in the installed schedule. A switching device is assessed only when the installed design documents one and exposes usable state/feedback evidence. The separately assessed outgoing-feeder protective device belongs to DQ-PDU-OUTGOING-FEEDER. No breaker tags, trip settings, curves, selectivity, ZSI behavior or internal topology are inferred.

questions.title: Is the documented PDU input, voltage conversion and internal protection available?
questions.applicability: Umbrella assessment for an identified PDU. It depends on separate incoming-supply, voltage-conversion and internal-protection evidence. Apply to an individual PDU only after its installed identity and upstream bus assignment are established from current site documentation.

questions.title: Is a documented PDU outgoing feeder available to supply its assigned SATS input?
questions.applicability: The historical description says each PDU feeds two SATS, but the generic graph does not identify individual PDU feeder-to-SATS assignments. Require current site drawings before applying to an installed feeder.

questions.title: Is the documented paired-PDU maintenance arrangement available for the intended maintenance state?
questions.applicability: The historical architecture describes PDUs paired to permit maintenance while maintaining power through the other PDU. It does not provide an individual pair map or authorize maintenance switching; verify site drawings and approved maintenance documentation.

questions.title: Are both documented independent source inputs available at the relevant SATS?
questions.applicability: The historical architecture describes two independent SATS sources associated with Critical Bus A and Critical Bus B. The generic model does not identify individual SATS inputs or PDU feeder assignments. Apply to an installed SATS only after current site drawings establish both input identities and assignments.

questions.title: Is the documented SATS sensing and automatic-transfer control function ready?
questions.applicability: Assess only the SATS control, sensing and operating-mode evidence exposed and documented for the identified unit. The historical description establishes automatic transfer as a function, but does not specify sensing thresholds, control-power architecture, logic equations, permissives, firmware behavior or test points.

questions.title: Is the documented SATS solid-state source-switching function available and responding to control?
questions.applicability: The source identifies SATS as solid-state automatic transfer switches but does not describe their internal power circuit. Assess only documented command, state/feedback, event and output evidence. Do not infer SCR/thyristor arrangement, semiconductor count, commutation circuit, overlap behavior, transfer-time acceptance limits or physical test points.

questions.title: Did the SATS respond to a documented loss of one source by transferring to the other source?
questions.applicability: The historical description states that SATS automatically transfers the load to the other source when one source fails. This question does not define sensing thresholds, transfer-time limits, detailed control logic, maintenance bypass behavior, or field switching procedures. Apply only with documented site-specific event and status evidence.

questions.title: Is a SATS supplying its load from an available intended source?
questions.applicability: The generic model contains only grouped PDU and SATS families. Apply to an individual SATS only after its installed identity, both input assignments and output assignment are established from current site documentation. No transfer thresholds, timing limits, or switching procedures are defined.

questions.title: Is the documented SATS-to-CDP incoming supply path available?
questions.applicability: The historical architecture describes SATS outputs feeding CDPs. The generic graph contains only grouped SATS and CDP families and an aggregate connection. Apply to an installed panel only after current site drawings establish the individual CDP identity and incoming assignment. No maintenance isolation or switching procedure is defined.

questions.title: Is a documented CDP outgoing branch circuit available to supply its assigned critical load?
questions.applicability: The historical architecture describes CDP panels feeding critical electronic/computer loads and identifies CDP observation at the panel and selected outgoing circuits. The generic graph contains no individual CDP tags, branch identities, protective-device assignments, or load schedule. Apply only after current site drawings and equipment schedules establish the installed branch and load.

questions.title: Is a CDP outgoing circuit unavailable?
questions.applicability: This is the umbrella CDP diagnosis. Localize the fault through the incoming-path and outgoing-branch questions; do not infer an installed circuit map from the generic architecture.

questions.title: Is the PMCS measurement channel reporting a valid instrument value?
questions.applicability: The source describes PowerLogic devices and measuring instruments but does not identify individual instruments, channels, signal wiring, calibration limits, or installed point tags. Apply only to a documented measurement point; no physical test terminal is defined.

questions.title: Has the PLC acquired the documented measurement or status signal correctly?
questions.applicability: The source identifies PLC and PMCS signal acquisition but provides no I/O list, channel numbers, PLC program mapping, or signal-level topology. These must be obtained from current site documentation before localizing an installed channel.

questions.title: Is the PLC data reaching the active OWS with valid communications and freshness?
questions.applicability: The source describes two redundant OWS stations with one active for control, plus communications networks and monitoring software. It does not define network topology, failover behavior, freshness thresholds, or point-level routing; do not infer these details.

questions.title: Does PMCS telemetry represent the physical equipment state?
questions.applicability: Umbrella assessment: combine the measurement-channel, PLC-acquisition and active-OWS communications/freshness assessments with DC control-power status and independent physical/electrical confirmation. A PMCS screen indication alone is not independent confirmation of physical equipment state. Signal-level topology and site-specific points remain unresolved.

questions.title: Is the documented load-bank test path in the intended source and switching state?
questions.applicability: Only when a documented generator or UPS load-bank test path is under review; this question does not define or authorize a test procedure.

questions.title: Is the documented SWGR control authority and operating mode consistent with the required transfer?
questions.applicability: The technical description identifies AUTO/LOCAL/MANUAL mode, PMCS command capability and local operation when PMCS is unavailable. The installed selector arrangement, authority arbitration and control logic require site drawings; no mode is presumed.

questions.title: Are the documented source, tie and interlock conditions satisfied for the required SWGR transfer?
questions.applicability: The source describes multiple breakers, switching conditions, delays and prohibitions on paralleling sources. Exact permissive equations, timer values, interlock topology and sequence are site-specific and are not encoded.

questions.title: Did the SWGR breaker execute the documented command and provide trustworthy position and electrical feedback?
questions.applicability: The source identifies command, control circuit, drive, physical contacts, position feedback and DC control power as distinct evidence. No breaker tags, coil ratings, terminal points, actuator design or field test procedure are inferred.

questions.title: Did the documented SWGR protective function detect the condition and produce the expected trip response?
questions.applicability: The historical technical description identifies voltage protection, time delays, shunt trip, undervoltage release and ZSI as protection/control functions. Assess only functions and event evidence documented for the identified installed SWGR. Separate condition detection, protective decision, trip output, breaker response and electrical interruption. Exact relay elements, thresholds, delays, trip-circuit design, device tags and test points require current site documents; this question defines no test or switching procedure.

questions.title: Does the documented SWGR protection response preserve the approved coordination and zone-selective behavior for the recorded event?
questions.applicability: The source describes time-current coordination and zone-selective interlocking, but installed settings and coordination are facility-specific. Compare an observed event only with the current approved site coordination study and installed device records. Do not calculate, recommend, infer or modify protection settings; no live fault test or switching procedure is defined.

questions.title: Did the documented SWGR under/overvoltage protection recognize the event and apply its configured time delay?
questions.applicability: The historical source describes minimum- and maximum-voltage protection with time delays. Assess only the installed voltage-protection functions documented for the identified switchgear and compare event evidence with the current approved settings record. Separate sensing validity, voltage condition, pickup, timer behavior and protection decision. Do not infer numeric thresholds, delay values, VT/fuse arrangement, relay model or test points. Breaker/trip execution is assessed separately under DQ-SWGR-PROTECTION-RESPONSE; this question defines no test or switching procedure.

global_constraints: A dependency is a prerequisite for interpreting evidence, not a proven physical causal edge.
Do not treat PMCS display state as independent proof of contact position or electrical condition.
Do not transform a logical observation template into a physical terminal or test point.
Do not invent individual device mappings inside grouped equipment families.
A missing prerequisite produces insufficient evidence, not an assumed healthy state.
Do not require generator readiness for a diagnosis under normal commercial-source operation; generator prerequisites apply only when standby operation or transfer is relevant.
Control-power availability is a separate evidence question; do not infer it from the commanded or displayed state of the equipment whose control function is under investigation.
Load-bank test-path questions describe architecture-level evidence only; they do not authorize switching, load testing, source paralleling, or field operations.
